literal: They were like wooden dogs or clay dragons; when names were checked against reality, the matter amounted to nothing.
idiomatic: They were no more real than wooden dogs or clay dragons—once names were matched to facts, the whole affair vanished into nothing.

literal: The consolidations now undertaken were to follow the separate regulations in every respect.
idiomatic: The consolidations now ordered were to follow the separate regulations in full.

literal: Thereupon three provinces, one hundred fifty-three commanderies, five hundred eighty-nine counties, two garrison-towns, and twenty-six outposts were merged and abolished.
idiomatic: Thereupon three provinces, 153 commanderies, 589 counties, two garrison-towns, and twenty-six outposts were merged away.

literal: It was further ordered that prefects and magistrates should all serve concurrently, without receiving stipends in kind.
idiomatic: It was further ordered that prefects and magistrates should all hold concurrent posts and receive no stipends in kind.

literal: In the twelfth month, Western Wei's Chancellor Yuwen Jue received Wei's abdication.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Western Wei's chancellor Yuwen Jue accepted the Wei abdication.

literal: Earlier, from the Zongqin Garrison in Xihe a Great Wall had been built eastward to the sea; in all, east and west, more than three thousand li had been constructed, with a fort roughly every ten li and garrison provinces or towns placed at key points—twenty-five in all.
idiomatic: Earlier, from the Zongqin Garrison in Xihe a Great Wall had been raised eastward to the sea; in all more than three thousand li had been built, with a fort roughly every ten li and garrison provinces or towns at the key points—twenty-five in all.

literal: In the third month of spring in the eighth year, the heat was extreme, and some people died of sunstroke.
idiomatic: In the third month of spring of the eighth year the heat was fierce, and some people died of sunstroke.

literal: On gengwu day in the fourth month of summer, an edict ordered that the taking of shrimp, crabs, clams, and the like should all cease; only fishing was permitted.
idiomatic: On gengwu day in the fourth month of summer an edict halted the taking of shrimp, crabs, clams, and the like; only fishing was allowed.

literal: On yiyou day, an edict likewise banned hawks and falcons, public and private.
idiomatic: On yiyou day an edict likewise banned hawks and falcons, whether public or private.

literal: Grand Preceptor and Prince Xianyang Hulü Jin was made Right Chancellor; former Grand General and Prince Fufeng Kezhuhun Daoyuan was made Grand Tutor; Helü Ren, Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, was made Grand Guardian; Prince Yan of Changshan, Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Minister of Works and recorder of the Masters of Writing; Prince Zhan of Changguang was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Yang Yin, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Left Vice Director; Cui Xian, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing for the consolidated offices, was made Right Vice Director; and Prince Huan of Shangdang was made recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Hulü Jin, grand preceptor and Prince of Xianyang, was made right chancellor; Kezhuhun Daoyuan, former grand general and Prince of Fufeng, grand tutor; Helü Ren, commissioner with protocol equal to the three excellencies, grand guardian; Prince Yan of Changshan, director of the Masters of Writing, minister of works and recorder of the Masters of Writing; Prince Zhan of Changguang, director of the Masters of Writing; Yang Yin, right vice director of the Masters of Writing, left vice director; Cui Xian, right vice director of the consolidated Masters of Writing, right vice director; and Prince Huan of Shangdang, recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: That month the Emperor held mounted archery east of the city and ordered all women of the capital to come and watch; those who failed to come were punished by military law; this lasted seven days before it stopped.
idiomatic: That month the emperor held mounted archery east of the city and commanded every woman of the capital to attend; those who stayed away were punished under military law, and the order lasted seven days.

literal: On xinyou day in the fifth month, Liu Xiang of Jizhou plotted rebellion in the capital; his accomplices were all executed.
idiomatic: On xinyou day in the fifth month Liu Xiang of Jizhou plotted rebellion in the capital, and his accomplices were all put to death.

literal: On jisi day in the eighth month of autumn, the Kumo Xi sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On jisi day in the eighth month of autumn the Kumo Xi sent envoys with tribute.

literal: On gengchen day, an edict ordered that for the mound, suburban, di, and ti sacrifices and seasonal rites, all offerings were to be purchased in the market; the young bullock might not be butchered on site, and officials were to supervise so that everything was fully provided.
idiomatic: On gengchen day an edict ordered that for the mound, suburban, di, and ti sacrifices and seasonal rites all offerings were to be bought in the market; the young bullock might not be butchered on the spot, and supervising officials were to see that everything was fully supplied.

literal: For the agricultural and sericulture rites, wine and meat alone sufficed.
idiomatic: For the agricultural and sericulture rites, wine and meat alone were enough.

literal: For the rain, marriage, wind, and other rites, and for the Director of the People, Director of Emolument, Spirit Star, and miscellaneous sacrifices, fruit, cakes, wine, and dried meat were used.
idiomatic: For the rain, marriage, wind, and other rites, and for the Director of the People, Director of Emolument, Spirit Star, and miscellaneous sacrifices, fruit, cakes, wine, and dried meat were offered.

literal: Only sincerity and reverence were to be fully observed, with the same meaning as if the spirits were present.
idiomatic: Only sincerity and reverence were to be fully observed—the meaning was the same as if the spirits were truly present.

literal: From summer through the ninth month, great locust plagues struck the six provinces north of the Yellow River, the twelve provinces south of the Yellow River, and the eight commanderies of the capital region.
idiomatic: From summer through the ninth month great locust plagues struck the six provinces north of the Yellow River, the twelve provinces south of it, and the eight commanderies of the capital region.

literal: That month they flew as far as the capital, blotting out the sun, their sound like wind and rain.
idiomatic: That month they flew as far as the capital, blotting out the sun, with a sound like wind and rain.

literal: On jiachen day, an edict remitted rent in all places struck by locusts that year.
idiomatic: On jiachen day an edict remitted rent in every district struck by locusts that year.

literal: That month Zhou's regent Yuwen Hu killed his ruler Emperor Min and enthroned the emperor's younger brother Yu, who became Emperor Ming.
idiomatic: That month Northern Zhou's regent Yuwen Hu killed his sovereign Emperor Min and enthroned the emperor's younger brother Yu, who became Emperor Ming.

literal: On yihai day in the tenth month of winter, Chen Baxian murdered his ruler Fangzhi and enthroned himself, becoming Emperor Wu of Chen; he sent envoys declaring himself a vassal with tribute.
idiomatic: On yihai day in the tenth month of winter Chen Baxian murdered his sovereign Fangzhi and seized the throne as Emperor Wu of Chen, then sent envoys declaring vassalage and tribute.

literal: That year, within the Great Wall a second wall was built from Kuluo Valley eastward to the Wuge Garrison, more than four hundred li in all.
idiomatic: That year a second wall was built inside the Great Wall from Kuluo Valley eastward to Wuge Garrison, more than four hundred li in all.

literal: In the second month of spring in the ninth year, on dinghai day, the sentences of convicts were reduced.
idiomatic: In the second month of spring of the ninth year, on dinghai day, the sentences of convicts were reduced.

literal: On jichou day, an edict limited the burning of fields to the mid-winter month and forbade setting fires at other times, lest insects and vegetation be harmed.
idiomatic: On jichou day an edict limited field-burning to the mid-winter month and forbade fires at other times, lest insects and plants be harmed.

literal: On dingyou day in the third month, the Emperor returned from Jinyang.
idiomatic: On dingyou day in the third month the emperor returned from Jinyang.

literal: On xinsi day in the fourth month of summer, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
idiomatic: On xinsi day in the fourth month of summer a general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: That summer there was a great drought.
idiomatic: That summer brought a great drought.

literal: Because prayers for rain went unanswered, the Emperor destroyed the shrine of Ximen Bao and dug up his tomb.
idiomatic: When prayers for rain went unanswered, the emperor destroyed the shrine of Ximen Bao and dug up his tomb.

literal: In Shandong there was a great locust plague; corvée laborers were dispatched to catch the insects and bury them in pits.
idiomatic: In Shandong a great locust plague struck, and corvée laborers were sent to catch the insects and bury them in pits.

literal: That month Sima Xiaonan, governor of Northern Yuzhou, rebelled with his city and went over to Zhou.
idiomatic: That month Sima Xiaonan, governor of Northern Yuzhou, rebelled with his city and defected to Northern Zhou.

literal: On xinchou day in the fifth month, Prince Zhan of Changguang, Director of the Masters of Writing, was made recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, General of Agile Cavalry, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: On xinchou day in the fifth month Prince Zhan of Changguang, director of the Masters of Writing, was made recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, general of agile cavalry, left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: On jiachen day, former Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: On jiachen day former left vice director of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin was made director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: On yichou day in the sixth month, the Emperor toured north from Jinyang.
idiomatic: On yichou day in the sixth month the emperor set out on a northern tour from Jinyang.

literal: On jisi day he reached Qilian Pool.
idiomatic: On jisi day he reached Qilian Pool.

literal: On wuyin day he returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: On wuyin day he returned to Jinyang.

literal: On xinchou day in the seventh month of autumn, nine hundred forty-three elderly men of the capital region, including Liu Nu, were granted office tablets, canes, and caps in varying measure.
idiomatic: On xinchou day in the seventh month of autumn 943 elderly men of the capital region, including Liu Nu, were granted office tablets, canes, and caps in varying measure.

literal: On wushen day, an edict remitted this year's rent and tax for fields damaged by locusts and floods last year in the five provinces of Zhao, Yan, Ying, Ding, and Southern Camp, and in the two commanderies of Guangping and Qinghe in Sizhou, as well as for fields whose crops were thin because spring and summer had brought little rain.
idiomatic: On wushen day an edict remitted this year's rent and tax for fields in Zhao, Yan, Ying, Ding, and Southern Camp and in Guangping and Qinghe in Sizhou that had been damaged by locusts and floods the year before, and for fields whose crops were thin after a dry spring and summer.

literal: On yichou day in the eighth month, he returned from Jinyang.
idiomatic: On yichou day in the eighth month he returned from Jinyang.

literal: On jiaxu day, the Emperor went to Jinyang.
idiomatic: On jiaxu day the emperor went to Jinyang.

literal: That month Shen Tai, governor of Jiangzhou in Chen, came over with three thousand men.
idiomatic: That month Shen Tai, Chen's governor of Jiangzhou, defected with three thousand men.

literal: Earlier, more than three hundred thousand corvée laborers and artisans had been mobilized to build the Three Towers below Ye on the old foundations, raising them higher and broader, and to construct great palaces and pleasure gardens.
idiomatic: Earlier more than three hundred thousand corvée laborers and artisans had been mobilized to build the Three Towers below Ye on their old foundations, raising them higher and broader, and to erect great palaces and pleasure gardens.

literal: By this time the Three Towers were complete; Copper Sparrow was renamed Golden Phoenix, Golden Beast was renamed Holy Response, and Ice Well was renamed Glorious Light.
idiomatic: By then the Three Towers were finished: Copper Sparrow was renamed Golden Phoenix, Golden Beast Holy Response, and Ice Well Glorious Light.

literal: On jiawu day in the eleventh month, the Emperor returned from Jinyang, ascended the Three Towers, presided in the Qianxiang Hall, held court and feasted the hundred officials, and ordered them all to compose poems.
idiomatic: On jiawu day in the eleventh month the emperor returned from Jinyang, ascended the Three Towers, presided in Qianxiang Hall, held court and feasted the hundred officials, and ordered them all to compose poems.

literal: Because the new palace was complete, on dingyou day a general amnesty was proclaimed, and civil and military officials within and without were universally promoted one full rank.
idiomatic: With the new palace complete, on dingyou day a general amnesty was proclaimed and every civil and military official within and without the court was promoted one full rank.

literal: On dingsi day, Wang Lin, governor of Xiangzhou in Liang, sent envoys asking that Xiao Zhuang be established as ruler of Liang, with Jiangzhou submitted to Qi and Zhuang installed there.
idiomatic: On dingsi day Wang Lin, Liang's governor of Xiangzhou, sent envoys asking that Xiao Zhuang be established as ruler of Liang, with Jiangzhou submitted to Qi and Zhuang installed there.

literal: On guiyou day in the twelfth month, an edict established Xiao Zhuang as ruler of Liang and had him advance to Jiupai.
idiomatic: On guiyou day in the twelfth month an edict established Xiao Zhuang as ruler of Liang and had him advance to Jiupai.

literal: On wuyin day, Grand Tutor Kezhuhun Daoyuan was promoted to Grand Preceptor; Minister over the Masses Wei Can was made Grand Commandant; Duan Shao, governor of Jizhou, was made Minister of Works; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the Masters of Writing, was made Grand Marshal; and Prince Zhan of Changguang, recorder of the Masters of Writing, was made Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: On wuyin day Grand Tutor Kezhuhun Daoyuan was promoted to grand preceptor; Minister over the Masses Wei Can, grand commandant; Duan Shao, governor of Jizhou, minister of works; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the Masters of Writing, grand marshal; and Prince Zhan of Changguang, recorder of the Masters of Writing, minister over the masses.

literal: That month construction began on the Great Solemnity Temple.
idiomatic: That month construction began on the Great Solemnity Temple.

literal: That year Prince Jun of Yong'an and Prince Huan of Shangdang were killed.
idiomatic: That year Prince Jun of Yong'an and Prince Huan of Shangdang were put to death.

literal: In the first month of spring in the tenth year, on wuxu day, Houmochen Xiang, Minister of Works, was made Grand General.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the tenth year, on wuxu day, Minister of Works Houmochen Xiang was made grand general.

literal: On jiayin day, the Emperor went to the Sweet Dew Temple at Liaoyang.
idiomatic: On jiayin day the emperor went to Sweet Dew Temple at Liaoyang.

literal: On yimao day, an edict established Hengzhou at Macheng.
idiomatic: On yimao day an edict established Hengzhou at Macheng.

literal: On bingxu day in the second month, the Emperor took up Chan retreat at Sweet Dew Temple in deep contemplation; only great affairs of state and the army were reported to him.
idiomatic: On bingxu day in the second month the emperor withdrew to Sweet Dew Temple for Chan retreat and deep contemplation; only great affairs of state and the army were reported to him.

literal: On wuxu day in the third month, Palace Attendant Gao Dezheng was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: On wuxu day in the third month Palace Attendant Gao Dezheng was made right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: On bingchen day, the Emperor returned from Liaoyang.
idiomatic: On bingchen day the emperor returned from Liaoyang.

literal: That month the Liang ruler Xiao Zhuang reached Yingzhou and sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That month the Liang ruler Xiao Zhuang reached Yingzhou and sent envoys with tribute.

literal: In the intercalary fourth month, on dingyou day, Prince You of Pengcheng, governor of Sizhou, was made Minister of Works, and Palace Attendant Prince Shi of Gaoyang was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month, on dingyou day, Prince You of Pengcheng, governor of Sizhou, was made minister of works, and Palace Attendant Prince Shi of Gaoyang, right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: On yisi day, Prince You of Pengcheng, Minister of Works, was additionally made Grand Commandant, and the emperor's son Shaoqian was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle Commandery.
idiomatic: On yisi day Prince You of Pengcheng, minister of works, was additionally made grand commandant, and the emperor's son Shaoqian was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle Commandery.

literal: On guiwei day in the fifth month, twenty-five households of the Yuan clan, including Shixi of the Western Capital and Jingshi of the Eastern Capital, were executed, and nineteen households including Special Advance Yuan Shao were placed under restriction.
idiomatic: On guiwei day in the fifth month twenty-five households of the Yuan clan, including Shixi of the Western Capital and Jingshi of the Eastern Capital, were executed, and nineteen households including Special Advance Yuan Shao were placed under restriction.

literal: In the sixth month, Emperor Wu of Chen died; his elder brother's son Qian succeeded him, becoming Emperor Wen.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Emperor Wu of Chen died; his elder brother's son Qian succeeded him as Emperor Wen.

literal: On wuxu day in the eighth month of autumn, the emperor's son Shaoyi was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang Commandery, and Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Left Vice Director.
idiomatic: On wuxu day in the eighth month of autumn the emperor's son Shaoyi was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang Commandery, and Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, right vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made left vice director.

literal: On guimao day, an edict ordered that among soldiers and commoners any who had changed their surname to enter the Yuan clan by fraud, or who falsely claimed kinship and forgot to declare their original surname because they called themselves Yuan, regardless of how many generations had passed, were all permitted to restore their original surname.
idiomatic: On guimao day an edict ordered that soldiers and commoners who had changed their surname to pass as Yuan, or who falsely claimed kinship and forgot their original surname because they called themselves Yuan, were all permitted to restore their original surname, no matter how many generations had passed.

literal: On jisi day in the ninth month, the Emperor went to Jinyang.
idiomatic: On jisi day in the ninth month the emperor went to Jinyang.

literal: That month Li Huai'ze and Lu Renhui were sent as envoys to Xiao Zhuang.
idiomatic: That month Li Huai'ze and Lu Renhui were dispatched as envoys to Xiao Zhuang.

literal: On jiawu day in the tenth month of winter, the Emperor suddenly died in the Deyang Hall of Jinyang Palace; he was thirty-one.
idiomatic: On jiawu day in the tenth month of winter the emperor suddenly died in Deyang Hall of Jinyang Palace; he was thirty-one.

literal: The testamentary edict read: "All affairs of mourning shall follow austerity in every respect.
idiomatic: The testamentary edict read: "All affairs of mourning shall follow austerity in every respect.

literal: The three-year mourning, though called the fulfillment of ritual, had since Han emperor Wen's reign been curtailed and practiced from of old; its spirit still had standing and might be adopted alike, with the period of mourning fixed at thirty-six days.
idiomatic: The three-year mourning, though called the fulfillment of ritual, had since Emperor Wen of Han curtailed it and the practice had continued from of old; its spirit still stood and might be adopted alike, with mourning fixed at thirty-six days.

literal: The heir, the hundred officials, and all near and far, domestic and foreign, were to set aside private grief in obedience to the edict and observe public mourning throughout.
idiomatic: The heir, the hundred officials, and all near and far, at home and abroad, were to set aside private grief in obedience to the edict and observe public mourning throughout.

literal: " On guimao day mourning was announced and the body was laid out in Xuande Hall.
idiomatic: " On guimao day mourning was announced and the body was laid out in Xuande Hall.

literal: On xinwei day in the eleventh month, the coffin returned to the capital.
idiomatic: On xinwei day in the eleventh month the coffin returned to the capital.

literal: On yiyou day in the twelfth month, the body was interred in the hall before the Supreme Ultimate.
idiomatic: On yiyou day in the twelfth month the body was placed in the hall before the Supreme Ultimate.

literal: On bingchen day in the second month of the first year of Ganming, he was buried at Wuning Tomb, posthumously titled Emperor Wenxuan, with the temple name Weizong.
idiomatic: On bingchen day in the second month of the first year of Ganming he was buried at Wuning Tomb, posthumously titled Emperor Wenxuan, with the temple name Weizong.

literal: At the beginning of the Wuping era, the title was again changed to Wenxuan and the temple name to Xianzu.
idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wuping era the title was again changed to Wenxuan and the temple name to Xianzu.

literal: From youth the Emperor had great breadth of mind; his purpose and understanding were deep and keen; outwardly gentle, inwardly firm; bold and resolute in decision.
idiomatic: From youth the emperor had great breadth of mind; his purpose and understanding were deep and keen; outwardly gentle yet inwardly firm; bold and resolute in judgment.

literal: He was fond of administrative affairs by nature; measuring from beginning to end, he handled difficult and complex matters all day without weariness.
idiomatic: By nature he loved administrative work; tracing matters from beginning to end, he handled the most difficult and complex affairs all day without weariness.

literal: When he first ascended the throne, he gave his heart to statecraft, governing subordinates by law and putting fairness first.
idiomatic: When he first ascended the throne he gave his heart to statecraft, governing subordinates by law and putting fairness first.

literal: If anyone violated the statutes, even close kin or old merit-holders were shown no indulgence; within and without the court all was clear and quiet, and none failed to stand in reverent awe.
idiomatic: If anyone violated the statutes, even close kin or old merit-holders were shown no indulgence; within and without the court all was clear and quiet, and none failed to stand in reverent awe.

literal: As for military and state strategy, he decided alone in his breast; his designs were vast and far-reaching, and he had the great outline of a ruler.
idiomatic: In military and state strategy he decided alone in his breast; his designs were vast and far-reaching, and he had the great outline of a true sovereign.

literal: Because the three realms stood like tripods and the various tribes had not yet submitted, he repaired armor and weapons, drilled and selected soldiers, and stationed a hundred-company guard force among his personal attendants.
idiomatic: Because the three realms stood like tripods and the various tribes had not yet submitted, he repaired armor and weapons, drilled and selected soldiers, and stationed a hundred-company guard force among his personal attendants.

literal: Whenever he went to the battle line he personally faced arrows and stones; when blades crossed he feared only that the enemy in front were too few, and repeatedly braved hardship and danger, often achieving victory.
idiomatic: Whenever he went to the battle line he personally faced arrows and stones; when blades crossed he feared only that the enemy before him were too few, and repeatedly braved hardship and danger, often achieving victory.

literal: Once, while feasting on the Eastern Hill, because Guanlong was not yet pacified he threw down his cup in rage, summoned Wei Shou before him, and had an edict drafted on the spot to proclaim to far and near that he would campaign west.
idiomatic: Once, while feasting on the Eastern Hill, because Guanlong was not yet pacified he threw down his cup in rage, summoned Wei Shou before him, and had an edict drafted on the spot proclaiming to far and near that he would campaign west.

literal: That year Emperor Wen of Zhou died; the people of the west were shaken with fear, and plans to cross Long were often made.
idiomatic: That year Emperor Wen of Northern Zhou died; the people of the west were shaken with fear, and plans to cross Long were often made.

literal: After his campaigns conquered on four fronts and his might shook the barbarians and the Chinese, six or seven years later he grew proud of his achievements, lingered in dissipation, and indulged in lewdness and violence.
idiomatic: After his campaigns conquered on four fronts and his might shook barbarians and Chinese alike, six or seven years later he grew proud of his achievements, lingered in dissipation, and indulged in lewdness and violence.

literal: Sometimes he danced and sang himself without cease, from dawn through the night and on through the day.
idiomatic: Sometimes he danced and sang himself without cease, from dawn through the night and on through the day.

literal: Sometimes he bared his body, smeared on powder and rouge, let his hair hang loose in barbarian dress, and wore mixed garments of brocade.
idiomatic: Sometimes he bared his body, smeared on powder and rouge, let his hair hang loose in barbarian dress, and wore mixed garments of brocade.

literal: Drawing blade and bow, he roamed the markets and visited the mansions of meritorious kin morning and evening.
idiomatic: Blade drawn and bow in hand, he roamed the markets and visited the mansions of meritorious kin morning and evening.

literal: At times he rode camels, mules, oxen, and donkeys without saddle or bridle; in fierce summer heat or bitter winter cold, or baring himself at midday and riding stripped, his attendants could not endure it, yet the Emperor was entirely at ease.
idiomatic: At times he rode camels, mules, oxen, and donkeys without saddle or bridle; in fierce summer heat or bitter winter cold, or baring himself at midday and riding stripped, his attendants could not endure it, yet the emperor was entirely at ease.

literal: Relatives of merit, honored ministers, and close attendants were mixed together in his company without any distinction of rank.
idiomatic: Relatives of merit, honored ministers, and close attendants were mixed together in his company without any distinction of rank.

literal: He summoned licentious women and assigned them to his attendants, visiting them morning and evening for amusement.
idiomatic: He summoned licentious women and assigned them to his attendants, visiting them morning and evening for amusement.

literal: Of all the killings, many were ordered dismembered, or burned in fire, or cast into rivers.
idiomatic: Of all the killings, many were ordered dismembered, burned in fire, or cast into rivers.

literal: Deep drunkenness lasting long made him ever more frenzied and deluded; in his final years he constantly said he saw ghosts, and also that he heard strange sounds.
idiomatic: Deep drunkenness lasting long made him ever more frenzied and deluded; in his final years he constantly said he saw ghosts and heard strange sounds.

literal: If resentment took root in his heart, execution was inevitable; the Yuan of the imperial clan were all slaughtered, and Prince Jun of Yong'an and Prince Huan of Shangdang met cruel injustice; Gao Longzhi, Gao Dezheng, Du Bi, Wang Yuanjing, Li Qianzhi, and others were all harmed on false charges.
idiomatic: If resentment took root in his heart, execution was inevitable; the Yuan of the imperial clan were slaughtered wholesale, and Prince Jun of Yong'an and Prince Huan of Shangdang met cruel injustice; Gao Longzhi, Gao Dezheng, Du Bi, Wang Yuanjing, Li Qianzhi, and others were all destroyed on false charges.

literal: Once at Jinyang he playfully stabbed Supervisor Wei Ziyao with a spear, and Wei fell dead at once.
idiomatic: Once at Jinyang he playfully stabbed Supervisor Wei Ziyao with a spear, and Wei fell dead at once.

literal: Again, on the Great Light Hall of the Three Towers he sawed Supervisor Mu Song with a saw until he died.
idiomatic: Again, in Great Light Hall of the Three Towers he sawed Supervisor Mu Song with a saw until he died.

literal: Again, while visiting the residence of Kaifu Bao Xian, he called out Supervisor Han Ti, who was innocent, from among the crowd and beheaded him.
idiomatic: Again, while visiting the residence of Kaifu Bao Xian, he called out the innocent Supervisor Han Ti from among the crowd and beheaded him.

literal: The rest of the cruel excess was beyond counting.
idiomatic: The rest of the cruel excess was beyond counting.

literal: Court and countryside were filled with anguish; each nursed resentment and hatred.
idiomatic: Court and countryside were filled with anguish; each nursed resentment and hatred.

literal: Yet because he had always governed subordinates with stern decisiveness, and moreover possessed a silent memory of great strength, the hundred officials trembled with fear and dared not do wrong; civil and military close attendants did not know whether they would live to see the morrow.
idiomatic: Yet because he had always governed subordinates with stern decisiveness, and moreover possessed a silent memory of great strength, the hundred officials trembled with fear and dared not do wrong; civil and military close attendants did not know whether they would live to see the morrow.

literal: He also undertook many constructions; corvée labor multiplied throughout the realm, the whole state was thrown into turmoil, and public and private alike were worn out with toil.
idiomatic: He also undertook many constructions; corvée labor multiplied throughout the realm, the whole state was thrown into turmoil, and public and private alike were worn out with toil.
